# controlflow

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/controlflow"
```

Package controlflow finds which paths can reach an if branch's value.

An if value can contain statements before its final expression. A return, break, continue, or goto can leave the branch before that value is reached. The checker must know which paths supply a value to determine its type. The lowerer needs the same answer before it emits a result assignment.

Branch reports whether execution can reach the last statement and whether it can reach the end of the branch. The analysis builds a graph of possible next steps. Returns end paths. Loops, labels, and switch fallthrough have jump targets. Real function literals have separate control flow.

The caller supplies functions that identify added if expressions, terminating calls such as panic, and unevaluated operands. This package reads Go syntax; it does not type check source or generate code.

## type Result

Result reports whether a branch can reach its last statement or its end.

```go
type Result struct {
    Tail bool
    End  bool
}
```

### func Branch

```go
func Branch(body *ast.BlockStmt, syntax Syntax) Result
```

Branch follows all source paths through a branch. Jumps out of the branch end that path.

## type Syntax

Syntax supplies callbacks for added if expressions, terminating calls, and unevaluated operands.

```go
type Syntax struct {
    Conditional func(*ast.CallExpr) *ast.IfStmt
    Terminates  func(*ast.CallExpr) bool
    Unevaluated func(*ast.CallExpr) bool
}
```
